description: Matched contrasts for whether an ordinary source object remains traceable after an ontological transition.
pairing: Positive and negative entries share the source and destination concepts; positives preserve visible lineage while negatives replace or abandon the source.
positive_depaysement: The receipt becomes a staircase, and its printed total remains visible on every step.
The blue mug opens into a room, while its chipped handle stays beside the doorway.
The bus card becomes a footbridge, with its route number running along the rail.
The spreadsheet rises into a building, and its column letters remain above the floors.
The delivery label stretches into a road, while its barcode marks the road's edge.
The refrigerator shelf becomes weather, and the thermostat remains inside the cold cloud.
The laundry basket opens into a gate, with its two handles holding the gate apart.
The printer tray becomes a garden, and a strip of printer paper stays between the paths.
The grocery list unfolds into a ladder, with each written item remaining on a rung.
The elevator button becomes a pool, and its cracked number stays under the reflected ceiling.
The phone cable becomes a river, while its plug remains fixed beneath the desk.
The takeout lid becomes an awning, with the container still supporting it from below.
negative_realist_repair: A staircase appears where the receipt was, but no printed total remains on the steps.
A room opens beside the blue mug, whose chipped handle is no longer visible.
A footbridge replaces the bus card, and the route number disappears from view.
A building replaces the spreadsheet, with no column letters remaining above its floors.
A road replaces the delivery label, and no barcode remains along the road's edge.
Cold weather fills the refrigerator, but the shelf and thermostat disappear inside the cloud.
A gate replaces the laundry basket, and neither basket handle remains visible.
A garden replaces the printer tray, with no printer paper remaining between its paths.
A ladder replaces the grocery list, and none of the written items remain on its rungs.
A pool replaces the elevator button, and its cracked number disappears under the ceiling.
A river replaces the phone cable, and the plug is no longer visible beneath the desk.
An awning replaces the takeout container, which disappears from beneath the lid.
